verdict.rationale: Ramp's agent platform explicitly designs for recurring/background automation — the agent-identity model includes 'Long-running access — for background agents that run on a schedule,' and the AI-agent channels doc calls out the CLI as suited for 'scripted/scheduled workflows,' with --no-input/--agent JSON modes fit for cron-style invocation. Ramp also ships many internally automated recurring processes (auto top-up, hotel rebooking, recurring GL sync) and webhooks for event-driven triggers. However, there is no documented native scheduler, cron API, or UI for configuring arbitrary recurring jobs/workflows — scheduling is implied via external orchestration (cron + CLI/webhooks) rather than a first-class Ramp scheduling primitive. Missing for 10: a documented native job/workflow scheduler or cron API, explicit UI/API for defining recurring custom workflows, and independent evidence of scheduled agent workflows running successfully in practice.
